Fold $\triangle BEF$ inward along $EF$ to $\triangle B^{\prime}EF$, and connect $BB^{\prime}$, $B^{\prime}G$, and $GC$. What is the minimum value of $B^{\prime}G+GC$ when $BB^{\prime}$ is at its maximum?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, when the quadrilateral B$^{\prime}$EBF is a square, BB$^{\prime}$ is maximized. \\
$\therefore$ BE = BF, \\
$\because$ AE = BF, \\
$\therefore$ AE = BE, \\
$\therefore$ E, F are respectively the midpoints of sides AB, BC, \\
Draw a line through B$^{\prime}$ perpendicular to CD at point H, \\
Then AE = BE = BF = B$^{\prime}$H = CH = $\frac{1}{2}$ BC = 2, \\
Construct the symmetric point C$^{\prime}$ of C with respect to AD, and connect B$^{\prime}$C$^{\prime}$, GC$^{\prime}$, \\
$\therefore$ CG = GC$^{\prime}$, \\
$\therefore$ B$^{\prime}$G + GC = B$^{\prime}$G + GC$^{\prime}$ $\ge$ B$^{\prime}$C$^{\prime}$, that is, the minimum value of B$^{\prime}$G + GC is B$^{\prime}$C$^{\prime}$, \\
In the right triangle $\triangle$B$^{\prime}$C$^{\prime}$H, B$^{\prime}$H = 2, HC$^{\prime}$ = CC$^{\prime}$ − CH = 8 − 2 = 6, \\
By the Pythagorean theorem, B$^{\prime}$C$^{\prime}$ = $\sqrt{2^{2}+6^{2}} = 2\sqrt{10}$, \\
$\therefore$ The minimum value of B$^{\prime}$G + GC is $\boxed{2\sqrt{10}}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, the side length of square $ABCD$ is $4$, and $E$, $F$, $G$ are moving points on sides $AB$, $BC$, $AD$, respectively, with $AE=BF$. Fold $\triangle BEF$ inward along $EF$ to $\triangle B^{\prime}EF$, and connect $BB^{\prime}$, $B^{\prime}G$, and $GC$. What is the minimum value of $B^{\prime}G+GC$ when $BB^{\prime}$ is at its maximum?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, when the quadrilateral B$^{\prime}$EBF is a square, BB$^{\prime}$ is maximized. \\
$\therefore$ BE = BF, \\
$\because$ AE = BF, \\
$\therefore$ AE = BE, \\
$\therefore$ E, F are respectively the midpoints of sides AB, BC, \\
Draw a line through B$^{\prime}$ perpendicular to CD at point H, \\
Then AE = BE = BF = B$^{\prime}$H = CH = $\frac{1}{2}$ BC = 2, \\
Construct the symmetric point C$^{\prime}$ of C with respect to AD, and connect B$^{\prime}$C$^{\prime}$, GC$^{\prime}$, \\
$\therefore$ CG = GC$^{\prime}$, \\
$\therefore$ B$^{\prime}$G + GC = B$^{\prime}$G + GC$^{\prime}$ $\ge$ B$^{\prime}$C$^{\prime}$, that is, the minimum value of B$^{\prime}$G + GC is B$^{\prime}$C$^{\prime}$, \\
In the right triangle $\triangle$B$^{\prime}$C$^{\prime}$H, B$^{\prime}$H = 2, HC$^{\prime}$ = CC$^{\prime}$ − CH = 8 − 2 = 6, \\
By the Pythagorean theorem, B$^{\prime}$C$^{\prime}$ = $\sqrt{2^{2}+6^{2}} = 2\sqrt{10}$, \\
$\therefore$ The minimum value of B$^{\prime}$G + GC is $\boxed{2\sqrt{10}}$.
